name: PhylogenyPro
description: A self-contained, browser-based platform for molecular phylogenetics that takes a set of sequences from the alignment to the dated tree. It reads FASTA, PHYLIP, NEXUS, Clustal, MEGA and GenBank files and morphological matrices; aligns them with a progressive aligner that can work on codons, with manual editing and trimming of ambiguous blocks; carries the genome of each partition (chloroplast, mitochondrion, nuclear ribosomal, low-copy nuclear) into every later step; selects among 56 DNA models, twelve empirical amino-acid matrices and Mk/Mkv by AIC, AICc and BIC, with partition schemes by greedy merging; infers trees by parsimony, distance methods, maximum likelihood with NNI and SPR search, and Metropolis-coupled Bayesian MCMC, the last two in Web Workers; measures support by bootstrap, ultrafast bootstrap, SH-aLRT, aBayes and posterior probabilities, and compares topologies by the KH, SH and AU tests; tests the molecular clock and dates the tree by least squares, penalised likelihood or a relaxed clock with fossil calibrations on the geological time scale; fits models of diversification; reconstructs ancestral characters with stochastic mapping, BM/OU/EB, independent contrasts, PGLS, Blomberg's K and Pagel's lambda; reconstructs ancestral areas with DEC, DIVALIKE and BAYAREALIKE with and without founder-event speciation; and compares trees by five distances, concordance factors, quartets, split networks and ABBA-BABA. Throughout, an interpretation guide places each computed number on its own scale, and a calibration assistant turns a fossil, a geological event or a known rate into a prior and says what it means in years. It ends in a tree studio with pictures of the OTUs and clades and a cut into k groups, a figure studio that restyles every figure in the twelve blocks at once, figures at any resolution, a methods section written from what was actually run, and a reproducible package the program writes itself. Every block is checked against an independent implementation in R.
softwareRequirements: A modern web browser; no installation
